newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close at new high, LVMH jumps.
newsitem.headline: French shares close at new high, LVMH jumps.

text.p: French shares ended at a closing high on Wednesday, with strong gains in LVMH and SGS-Thomson, but were below an all-time high set earlier in the day.
Brokers said the continued strength of the dollar and gains on Wall Street as well as rises on other European market such as London were supporting the market.
The French government on Wednesday repaid 90.9 billion francs in so-called Balladur bonds and much of this liquidity is expected to end up in the share market.
The CAC-40 index closed up 37.31, or 1.26 percent, at 2,988.01. It set an all-time record at 2,998.28, within a whisper of the psychologically significant 3,000 level.
CAC-40 July futures ended at 2,998 vs 2,957 at Tuesday close.
The broader SBF-120 index closed up 24.31 at 2,039.36.
Volume was 10 billion francs of which 7.9 billion in CAC-40 shares.

LVMH closed up 3.10 percent at 1,628. Chairman Bernard Arnault detailed his plan for a drinks merger with Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc. In a first reaction the British groups called the deal "complicated and costly" but said they would study it.
Dealers said that the market could try and test the 3,000 level on Thursday.
"With all those favourable elements such as the rates, the dollar and the Balladur bond, we could have gone further. Especially when you look at other European bourses," a broker said.
The publication of a weaker-than-expected June U.S. CPI figure only briefly affected shares on Wednesday.
On Thursday, the French government will have a special meeting to discuss new budget measures which could be announced on Monday with the outcome of an audit into public finances.

Government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann had no comment on Wednesday after the regular cabinet meeting on a report in daily Le Monde saying corporate taxes would be raised for 1997 to help lower the budget deficit.
The Bank of France monetary council is meeting on Thursday and is expected to leave rates unchanged.
Car parts group Valeo reported a 12.8 percent rise in first half profits to 770 million francs after the close. The share had closed 2.77 percent higher at 412.10 francs.

Semi-conductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV, up 3.89 percent at 561 francs, build on Tuesday's gain ahead of its first half results on Thursday. Recent earnings reports from Intel Corp, Texas Instruments and Motorola have raised hopes for a good figure.
Insurance group GAN, up 6.03 percent at 146, is biggest riser of the day. La Tribune said negotiations between France and Brussels on recapitalisation are due to be finalised soon.
Eurotunnel, biggest faller with 3.65 percent fall at 6.60 francs, continues this week's decline.
AXA-UAP, up 2.86 percent at 384.60, biggest volume stock in a turnover of 786 million francs.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
